reason: Seawater can enter the seafloor through open fractures, starting the circulation loop.
expectation: Seawater will move down into the fractured rock.

effect: Seawater has entered the crust, so the next step is to heat it underground.
reaction: The circulation route is becoming clear.
reason: The infiltrating seawater can approach the hot rock beneath the seafloor.
expectation: The water will heat up as it circulates through the crust.

effect: The infiltrating water is now heated within the crust; the next part of its route is not yet clear.
reaction: The role of pressure in keeping the fluid below the surface is interesting.
reason: Checking the heated water's partners should reveal how it continues through the circulation loop.
expectation: The inspection will show what the heated water can interact with next.

effect: The inspection automatically continued the circulation: hot water reacted with buried rock and now carries dissolved material.
reaction: The exchange with rock makes the fluid's changing chemistry clearer.
reason: The hydrothermal fluid must return through the seafloor to reach the sea; inspecting it will reveal its available route.
expectation: The inspection will show how the fluid can continue toward the sea.

effect: The fluid is rising through fractures, driven by buoyancy and pressure differences.
reaction: It is useful to see that entry and return can occur through different fractures.
reason: The rising fluid should meet the surrounding seawater as it emerges.
expectation: The hot fluid will emerge and mix with cooler seawater, potentially depositing minerals.

effect: Mixing with cooler seawater caused minerals to precipitate at the vent; neither goal has yet been reported complete.
reaction: The link between cooling and mineral precipitation is useful.
reason: The precipitating minerals are the clearest starting point for building the vent deposit; inspecting them should reveal the next available step.
expectation: The inspection will show what can help the precipitated minerals form a deposit.

effect: The precipitated minerals formed a deposit around the outlet, completing the vent-deposit goal. Heated water still needs to return to the sea.
reaction: The modest deposit is a useful reminder that not every vent makes a towering chimney.
reason: The hot fluid has reached the outlet and should now enter the sea.
expectation: The heated fluid will return to the sea, completing the circulation goal.

effect: The hot fluid formed a hydrothermal plume, completing the circulation goal and the chapter.
reaction: The distinction between suspended minerals and smoke was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the water from heating through rock reactions to precipitation made the hydrothermal process understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: The successive inspections felt somewhat repetitive, although each revealed and automatically performed the next operation.

surprise.text: Water can enter and return through different fractures, and the visible plume is suspended mineral material rather than smoke.

arbitrary.text: Using the open fractures to build the deposit was not immediately obvious, though the result explained precipitation around an outlet.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow more linked natural processes, especially where the explanations distinguish the model from what is uncertain.
